adjudicated.jp: さてと。

adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 部活の方は、他の人々に任せて、と。
adjudicated.en: Club activities are left in the hands of others, so,
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 冬子を拾ってきますか。
adjudicated.en: shall I not go recover Touko?
comments: formal for some reason -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Taichi proposes going to pick Touko up. 'Recover Touko' treats her as a lost object or a rescue target.

highlights.text: shall I not go recover Touko?

adjudicated.jp: 車で行こう。
adjudicated.en: I'll go by car.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 職員室から鍵をあさり、合う車を探す。
adjudicated.en: I scrounged a key from the staff room, and I now search for the matching car.
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese gives a single present narrative sequence of rummaging for keys and finding the matching car. The English arbitrarily mixes past and present.

highlights.text: I scrounged a key from the staff room, and I now search for the matching car.

adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Ouch..."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 駐車場は惨劇になっていた。
adjudicated.en: A tragedy had taken place in the parking area.
adjudicated.assessment: The parking lot is described metaphorically as a scene of disaster. 'A tragedy had taken place' asserts an actual tragic event.

highlights.text: A tragedy had taken place in the parking area.

adjudicated.jp: まるで暴走車が、当て逃げを繰り返したみたいに。
adjudicated.en: It's as if a rampant driver had performed repeated hit-and-runs, over and over.
comments: 暴走. Remember it... -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The comparison is to a runaway or rampaging car repeatedly striking vehicles and fleeing. The English substitutes a 'rampant driver' and the formal criminal phrase 'performed hit-and-runs.'

highlights.text: It's as if a rampant driver had performed repeated hit-and-runs, over and over.

adjudicated.jp: 「全部凹んでる……」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "They're all dented..."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: こっちはバンパーがもげてる。
adjudicated.en: Here we have a torn-off bumper,
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 木が折れてる。
adjudicated.en: there a tree was splintered,
comments: Hard to tell without seeing much about the kind of trees, but if it were to be cut in half or something the odds the car would still work are low. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: フロントに放射状にヒビが。
adjudicated.en: cracks in that front radiator...
adjudicated.assessment: フロント here refers to the front glass or windshield bearing radiating cracks. A radiator does not take radial visible cracking in the described list, and the Japanese does not name one.

highlights.text: cracks in that front radiator...

adjudicated.jp: 「……友貴先生……」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "...Tomoki-sensei..."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 神々しいまでに運転の才能がない友貴だった。
adjudicated.en: Tomoki had a lack of driving talent that reached the divine.
comments: Literally, as he still drove off with what is implied to be zero instructions or practice at all. The reason he's "normal" is that he can learn to drive manual pretty damn quickly, all things considered. He shares this with Yutaka, who also has a foot on 'manual' (see CCA0011C, where this driving metaphor properly began). Sakuraba rides the bike, so it's unlikely he asked him. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「やっぱ素人にミッションは無理か、ククク」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Truly, amateurs on that 'mission aren't gonna make it, keh keh keh!"
comments: Mission OR transmission, see CCA0003 - amateurs rejected! -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: ミッション is Japanese automotive shorthand for a manual transmission, with a joke about an amateur handling it. Leaving it as English 'mission' loses the automotive meaning.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Truly, amateurs on that 'mission aren't gonna make it, keh keh keh!"

adjudicated.jp: そこへ行くと俺なんか、ちゃんと乗り方知ってるもんね。
adjudicated.en: When it comes to myself, however, I really know how to ride these things.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 人間としての格の違いってやつか。
adjudicated.en: Is it just the difference in our levels of humanity?
comments: 17% vs 84%. Likely. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: キーの合った車に乗り込む。
adjudicated.en: I get on the car that fits the key.
comments: The whole scene was massacred in the PS2 version because they removed him actually getting on a car and driving. Taichi, there, is apparently somehow driving his own self, and is utterly surreal idea. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: One gets into a car, not 'on the car.'

highlights.text: I get on the car that fits the key.

adjudicated.jp: 男だから当然ミッションだ。
adjudicated.en: I am a man, therefore the 'mission, naturally,
adjudicated.assessment: Taichi says that because he is a man, naturally the car is a manual transmission. The English uses the unrelated word 'mission' and leaves the sentence dangling into the punch line.

highlights.text: I am a man, therefore the 'mission, naturally,

adjudicated.jp: オートマ。

adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 女子供の乗り物だな。
adjudicated.en: It's a vehicle for women and children, they say.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「ケッ、見せてやるぜよ！」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Pah, I'm gonna show you now!"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 荒々しい俺だった。
adjudicated.en: I was rough and wild.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: ちょっと龍馬入ってる。
adjudicated.en: There's also a bit of the war horse, gallant in the face of battle.
comments: I can only suspect it's also a reference to [龍馬/竜馬]のつまずき, "even the best horse stumbles". -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: 龍馬 refers to Ryoma and explains Taichi's imitation of the distinctive ぜよ speech. The English translates the name's characters as a generic 'war horse' and invents a battle description.

highlights.text: There's also a bit of the war horse, gallant in the face of battle.

adjudicated.jp: 半クラッチから見事にアクセルを繋いだ。
adjudicated.en: I magnificently accelerate from a half-clutch position.
comments: That's a manual gear driving technique. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: いかん、目の前の車にぶつけてしまった。
adjudicated.en: Dammit, I just bumped into that car in front of me!
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: シートベルトしててよかった。
adjudicated.en: Good thing I fastened my seatbelt.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: とりあえず後退しよう。
adjudicated.en: For now let's back out.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「バック石松、バック石松っと……」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Back Isshimatsu, Back Isshimatsu, and..."
comments: Can't find anything but a pun on this: http://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E3%82%AC%E3%83%83%E3%83%84%E7%9F%B3%E6%9D%BE (English term returns it within first few results) -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: タイヤ止めを乗り越えて背後の樹木をへし折ってしまったぞ。
adjudicated.en: Overcoming the tire stops I break into the shrubbery on the back.
comments: I think it's just part of the parking space, only specifically intended to prevent, well, the above. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The car crosses the wheel stop and snaps the tree behind it. The English changes the tree into shrubbery and merely says that the car breaks into it.

highlights.text: Overcoming the tire stops I break into the shrubbery on the back.

adjudicated.jp: 「バッドだぜ～」

adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.en: This kind of mistake isn't a one in a million. A Hyper Rare Event.
adjudicated.assessment: Taichi says that this mistake would not happen even once in a million times and calls it hyper-rare. 'Isn't a one in a million' normally denies that it is rare and contradicts the next sentence.

highlights.text: This kind of mistake isn't a one in a million. A Hyper Rare Event.

adjudicated.jp: リトライ。
adjudicated.en: Reee-try.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: しまった、ギアがバックのままだった。
adjudicated.en: Dammit, it was still in reverse gear.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 百万分の一に百万分の一をかけると……いくつだ。
adjudicated.en: Multiply one in a million by one in a million... how much's even that.
comments: Either 1 in a billion or 2 in a hundred. Dunno; math is hard. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: まあいい。
adjudicated.en: Ah, who cares.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: きらめくほどに俺は奇跡的なのだ。
adjudicated.en: I'm so miraculous I could just sparkle.

adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 高そうな車なのに……すまん、今は亡き榊原教諭。
adjudicated.en: And that car even looks so expensive... sorry, Currently-Deceased Professor Sakakibara.
adjudicated.assessment: 今は亡き is the conventional 'late' for a deceased person, and 教諭 is a teacher. 'Currently-Deceased Professor' is an unnatural, comic bureaucratic construction not present in the Japanese.

highlights.text: And that car even looks so expensive... sorry, Currently-Deceased Professor Sakakibara.

adjudicated.jp: 前に出る。
adjudicated.en: I head forwards.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: おっとっと、サイドブレーキ入れたままだった。
adjudicated.en: Whoa, whoa, woah the handbrake was still engaged.
comments: He had to have pressed that accelerator down to the metal to get it to move at all so far. Handbrake is "sidebrake" in Japanese, so in the PS2 version it reads "the side was still engaged". WTF. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 戻す。
adjudicated.en: Disengage.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: がくん、と車が急加速する。
adjudicated.en: Boom, the car accelerates suddenly.
comments: Although automatic cars crawl forwards when not in brake, he likely had the accelerator down. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: がくん describes the car lurching as it accelerates. 'Boom' introduces an explosive sound.

highlights.text: Boom, the car accelerates suddenly.

adjudicated.jp: 横一列に並んでいた車の鼻先をかすめながら、バンパーをもぎっていく。
adjudicated.en: Grazing the noses of the cars parked in the rows, and ripping off the bumper.
adjudicated.assessment: The car clips the noses of vehicles lined in a single row and tears off their bumpers as it goes. The English changes the row to plural rows and leaves a single bumper without a clear owner.

highlights.text: Grazing the noses of the cars parked in the rows, and ripping off the bumper.

adjudicated.jp: かなり効率よく破壊してしまったぞ。
adjudicated.en: I'm pretty efficient at destruction dammit.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: やべー、校長のフェラーリもひどいことに。
adjudicated.en: No waaay, I did something really nasty to the headmaster's Ferrari.
comments: Shinkawa's catchphrase... PS2 version talks about "that expensive war horse". ...then again, since this likely happens only in his mind... -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The narrator observes that the principal's Ferrari is now in terrible condition too. The English explicitly makes him the agent and describes an intentionally 'nasty' act.

highlights.text: No waaay, I did something really nasty to the headmaster's Ferrari.

adjudicated.en: Taichi: "..."
adjudicated.assessment: The source text has multiple authoritative occurrences and this unit lacks a unique binding.

highlights.text: Taichi: "..."

adjudicated.jp: ま、いっか。こんな危険な学校でフェラる方が悪い。
adjudicated.en: Ah, who cares. F'ing in this dangerous school is improper.
comments: ※フェラる＝太一語。二つの意味が。①フェラーリのオーナーになること。②（全略）
I guess it now sounds more like 'fucking' than 'fellatio', but, eh, who gives a blowjob. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese pun blames the person who brings or drives a Ferrari at such a dangerous school. The English turns the pun into an unrelated claim that sexual activity at school is improper.

highlights.text: Ah, who cares. F'ing in this dangerous school is improper.

adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「しかし日本車のもろいことよ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "But damn, Japanese cars are so fragile!"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: こんな車で西部の警察に配属されることなど、夢のまた夢。
adjudicated.en: The idea that this car would ever be deployed to the police in the West is but dream within dream.
adjudicated.assessment: 西部の警察 functions as a named or pop-cultural police reference in the car-destruction joke, not an ordinary geographic description of police somewhere in 'the West.'

highlights.text: The idea that this car would ever be deployed to the police in the West is but dream within dream.

adjudicated.jp: せいぜいが放水車で破壊されるが関の山。
adjudicated.en: The best they could do is get wrecked by water cannon fire engines, and no more.
comments: Term's relatively generic, but: http://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E7%A0%B4%E5%A3%8A%E6%A9%9F%E6%95%91%E9%9B%A3%E6%B6%88%E9%98%B2%E8%BB%8A <- guessing. It sounds like a movie reference, no idea. Some of those fire engines that I see GISing around look like they could just trample on cars, too. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The car's best prospect is to end up destroyed by a water-cannon truck. 'Water cannon fire engines' conflates vehicle types and changes the singular car into plural 'they.'

highlights.text: The best they could do is get wrecked by water cannon fire engines, and no more.

adjudicated.jp: 地面に『の』の字を書きながら待っていると、奥からするすると車が走ってきた。

adjudicated.assessment: Drawing の on the ground conventionally depicts dejection or sulking in this context. The English labels the gesture embarrassment and adds a spiraling motion not stated by the source.

highlights.text: I pass the time by embarrassedly spiraling my finger in the ground in the shape of the 'no' hiragana, until a car came smoothly riding out from the back.

adjudicated.assessment: Youko drives smoothly and stops before Taichi. 'Driving without hesitation, it stops' attaches the human action of driving to the car.

highlights.text: Driving without hesitation, it stops right in front of me.

adjudicated.jp: 「乗って」

highlights.text: Taichi: "...castle Kirihara, if I may graciously impose."

adjudicated.en: And so it was that I became filled with sad feelings.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.
